# Effect: auto_pan

Auto-pan: moves the sound back and forth between left and right with an LFO.

**Where to put it**: Good for pad, arpeggios and percussion accents; do not use on bass or kick. To sync to the beat: rate_hz = tempo / 60 / beats.

Latest parameters: `muser effects auto_pan` (MCP: `describe_effect`)

## Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `shape` | `sine` | `sine` / `triangle` / `square` / `saw_up` / `saw_down` | LFO waveform: sine is smooth; square jumps between left and right |
| `rate_hz` | 0.5 | 0 – 40 Hz | Movement rate. 0.1-0.5 slow drift; above 2 fast swaying |
| `width` | 1 | 0 – 1 | Swing width. 1 goes from full left to full right; 0.3 stays near the center |

All parameters can be omitted and take their default when omitted; when a value is out of range, `muser validate` reports the exact location.

## Minimal example

```json
{ "type": "auto_pan", "rate_hz": 0.25, "width": 0.8 }
```

## Scenario presets

- Slowly drifting pad

  ```json
  {"type": "auto_pan", "rate_hz": 0.15, "width": 0.7}
  ```

- Swing left and right by the bar @120bpm (once every 2 beats = tempo/120)

  ```json
  {"type": "auto_pan", "rate_hz": 1, "width": 1}
  ```

- Percussion accent that jumps left and right

  ```json
  {"type": "auto_pan", "rate_hz": 2, "width": 0.8, "shape": "square"}
  ```

## Tips and common mistakes

- Keep bass, kick and lead vocal in the center; do not auto-pan them.
- When several tracks all move, staggering the rates (0.13, 0.21...) is more natural than using the same rate.
